Whether you’re stocking up on holiday gifts or adding to your own collection, here are some favorite cookbooks from me and other BA staffers on sale right now.
Ottolenghi Simple by Yotam Ottolenghi (53% off)

This is undoubtedly my favorite and most cooked from cookbook, and it’s on sale right now for the price of two morning matchas, or a Domino’s pizza, or a jar of nut butter—you get the picture. Simple is filled with recipes that are equally suitable for weeknight dinners (hence the book’s name) as they are for entertaining. Certain recipes—like the Hot Charred Cherry Tomatoes With Cold Yogurt—have become staples in my own house, while others I’ve got bookmarked for my next summer dinner party (I’m looking at you, Vanilla Custard With Roasted Strawberries And Rhubarb).

Design and photography nerds will appreciate the book’s beautiful layout, fun use of color, and stunning images; but this is, crucially, not the kind of book made just to look at. It’s a book you’ll end up cooking from constantly—if you’re anything like me, anyway.
Dac Biet by Nini Nguyen (64% off)

blocks.x: Dac Biet: An Extra-Special Vietnamese Cookbook

I’m in a cookbook club with fellow NYC food editors in which we cook from a new book each month. After our potluck-style meal from Nini Nguyen’s Dac Biet (you might know her from Top Chef or Tournament of Champions), we all agreed: This was the best one our club had tried to date.

In her debut cookbook, Nguyen blends Vietnamese roots with her New Orleans upbringing, creating deeply flavorful recipes that are both comforting and surprising. Bon Appétit’s senior cooking editor Kelsey Youngman made the Pork Ribs Glazed With Roasted Nuoc Mam Sauce—they were tender and sweet and funky (from the brown sugar and fish sauce), and no grill was required. Just three hours in the oven and a quick broil. I made the Soy Sauce Chicken, which delivered juicy, umami-rich thighs with perfectly caramelized skin, and it’s since become a weeknight staple.

You’ll also find Southern-Vietnamese mash-ups like Southeast Asian Jambalaya, in which lemongrass, lime leaves, and Thai basil meet bell pepper and Creole seasoning. Dac Biet is exactly what it promises: extra special. —Olivia Tarantino, senior commerce editor

The hardcover version (the best version of any cookbook) is almost 50% off right now. —Noah Kaufman, senior reviews editor
Salad Freak by Jess Damuck (49% off)

blocks.c: Image may contain: Cutlery, Fork, Advertisement, Food, Fruit, Plant, Produce, and Poster

blocks.x: Salad Freak: Recipes to Feed a Healthy Obsession

A cookbook on salads was the last thing I thought I needed. I know how to make a salad. You know how to make a salad. We all know how to make a salad. But Jess Damuck’s Salad Freak proved me wrong. Over the years, it’s turned into one of the most-grabbed books on my overcrowded shelf. Damuck is a food stylist, so it goes without saying that the recipes are pretty. Endive petals dripping in vinaigrette. Rainbow tomatoes and oozing burrata. Cantaloupe slices covered in crushed ice. But there is substance amid all the beauty. A yogurt dressing I’ve practically memorized. An herby, olive-y romaine salad that’s become my go-to contribution to potlucks. Being organized by season makes the book practical and highly usable, whether you can’t pick between the bounty of the summer farmers market or are in need of something fresh in the dead of winter. Plus: The title! —Emma Laperruque, cooking director
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6a3a9bef2ad1f98c2a0fc83f/master/w_1600%2Cc_limit/IMG_0637.jpeg
Chopped Cucumber and Feta Salad, pre-feta.
Emma Laperruque
By Heart by Hailee Catalano (43% off)
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/67e7003223b988060207480e/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Screenshot%25202025-03-24%2520at%252011.25.38%2520AM.png
blocks.c: Image may contain: Advertisement, Poster, People, and Person

blocks.x: By Heart: Recipes to Hold Near and Dear

Hailee Catalano’s debut cookbook, By Heart, feels instantly essential because it takes classic, unfussy dishes and elevates them just enough to make them feel special without becoming intimidating. Her Roast Chicken with Red Wine Vinegar and Honey takes a familiar roast chicken up a notch by calling for browning the spatchcocked bird before roasting and finishing it with a simple pan sauce. The same approach shines in the recipe for Mustardy Herb-Buttered Potatoes, which transforms a humble boiled potato with butter, mustard, and herbs. Throughout the book, Catalano strikes a balance that many cooks aspire to: recipes that are approachable yet thoughtful, with just enough technique to add an extra dimension of flavor. Her love of seasonal ingredients comes through in dishes like Grated Tomato Linguine, which captures exactly what you want to eat at the height of tomato season. Hailee is a chef you want to root for, and it’s made even easier by the fact that her recipes are actually this good. —Emma Jacobson, social media editor
100 Cookies by Sarah Kieffer (43% off)
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/686fef69d845fde014fcee3a/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/100-cookies-cookbook.jpg
blocks.c: Image may contain: Food, Sweets, Bread, Cream, Dessert, and Ice Cream

blocks.x: 100 Cookies: The Baking Book for Every Kitchen

You may know Sarah Kieffer from her lauded The Vanilla Bean Blog or for popularizing a pan-banging cookie technique that went viral around 2017. 100 Cookies has a whole chapter dedicated to those perfectly textured, beautifully rippled treats. There’s a recipe for classic chocolate chip, of course, but also others like Rocky Road, Ginger Molasses, S’mores, and my favorite, the Toasted Sesame. In the other chapters, you’ll find recipes like Banana Crunch Blondies, Cream Cheese Pumpkin Pie Bars, and Meringues with Cacao Nibs and Caramel Swirl.
